title: Automated qualitative batch measurement of lipid droplets in the liver of bird using ImageJ
protocol: Click on "Connect" and enable emission to turn the laser system on.
Configure the ULPING system parameters based on the desired electrode characteristics.
Adjust the scan speed parameter of the laser system in the property table tab.
Determine the precise location and focal length for irradiation using the marking preview dashboard.
Open the Marking Mate 2.7 CAD software.
Click on "New File" and select "Rectangle Shape" from the left ribbon (Draw).
Draw a rectangle profile.
Click on "View" to activate the Property Table tab.
Under the "Frame/Fill" tab, select the desired pitch pattern from the "Style" icon.
Under the "Rectangle" tab, select the laser scan speed from the "Speed" icon.
Press the F5 button on the keyboard to enable the marking preview dashboard.
Preview the location of the irradiation and focal length of the laser beam on the sample by clicking on "Preview".
When satisfied with the preview, deactivate it and initiate the ULPING process by clicking on "Exec".
Monitor the fabrication process closely to ensure the desired electrode morphology and integrity are achieved.
Cut the obtained TiO electrode samples into smaller sections.
Use a punch tool to create 6 mm diameter holes in the Ti sheets.
Each circular disc should have an area of 27.2 mm².
Place the TiO electrode in the lower case of the coin cell.
Add the electrolyte solution and separator to the coin cell, ensuring proper separation between the electrodes.
Position the second TiO electrode on top of the separator, creating a sandwich-like structure with the lower TiO electrode.
Place the upper case onto the coin cell assembly and securely fasten it.
Connect the potentiostat cables to the appropriate terminals on the coin cell.
Prepare the 1 M sodium sulfate electrolyte in a common manner, following standard protocols.
Perform CV tests on the coin cell configurations.
Conduct CV tests at scan rates of 500 mV/s (with a stable potential range of -1 V to 1 V) and 50 mV/s (with a stable potential range of −0.8 V to 0.8 V).
Carry out GCD experiments on the coin cell configurations.
Perform GCD experiments at potentials ranging from −0.8 V to 0.8 V, with current densities ranging from 0.25 mA/cm².
Perform EIS testing on the coin cell configurations.
Conduct EIS testing at a perturbation voltage of 50 mV/s.
Measure frequencies ranging from 100 mHz to 100 kHz.
Record laser fabrication parameters for both base and changing electrodes.
Classify recorded quantitative values into three groups.
Note the power (W) during laser fabrication.
Document frequency (kHz) used in laser fabrication.
Capture pulse duration (ps-ns) in laser fabrication.
Track scan speed (mm/s) during laser fabrication.
Collect electrochemical numeric results.
Position electrode P1 in the lower cover of the MTI coin cell setup.
Place an identical P1 electrode on top.
Repeat this procedure 30 more times with P1 as the base electrode and different electrodes on top.
Perform tests on test electrode P2, including self-tests and tests against other electrodes except P1.
Continue testing until reaching the final 31st electrode, ensuring each is tested only once against itself.
Assemble all 496 sets of electrodes based on the mix-and-match testing matrix.
Create a new Excel file named "test1."
Paste selected data from OriginPro into "test1" for further manipulation.
Launch MATLAB and open a new script (Ctrl+N) to perform calculations.
Interpret the obtained results.
Record the interpreted results for further analysis and scientific documentation.
Use MATLAB code to calculate specific areal capacitance and discharge time for all 496 sets.
Analyze calculated specific areal capacitance and discharge time values using the MATLAB code.
Interpret and record results obtained from analysis.
Load parameters such as capacity, impedance, phase angle, and real impedance at lower and higher frequencies into OriginPro using BioLogic connector.
Include final dataset of parameters for further analysis.
Utilize SEM and EDX equipment to obtain numeric results for oxidation percentage and Ti/oxidation ratio for both electrodes.
Measure porosity using ImageJ software.
Load the desired image for porosity measurement.
Select "Image" > "Type" > "RGB Color".
Select "Image" > "Color" > "Split channels".
Choose the channel with the most contrast and highest quality for SEM images.
Use the rectangular selection tool to choose the largest rectangular section of the coating, excluding any interfaces.
Use the threshold tool to identify porosity areas.
Select "Image" > "Adjust" > "Threshold" or press "Ctrl+Shift+X".
Drag both slider bars to the far left to set them both to zero.
Increase the value of the bottom slider gradually to highlight the dark porosity patches.
Select "Apply" in the threshold menu to convert the image into a binary representation of porosity.
Click "Analyze" > "Analyze Particles."
Ensure that only the "Display Results" box is checked, and click "OK."
Uncheck the “display results” and check the “summarize box.”
Copy the area fraction value from the summary into an Excel spreadsheet.
Repeat this analysis 3 times for each image.
Calculate the porosity of the sample by averaging the area fraction values for all images analyzed.
Record and document the results of the porosity analysis.
Separate the independent variables (X) and the target variable (y) using the `separate_it()` function.
Split the data into training and test sets using the `train_test_split()` function.
Define the Adam optimizer with the specified learning rate.
Build the MLP model using the Sequential API.
Compile the model with the Adam optimizer, mean squared error loss, and mean squared error metric.
Train the model on the training data and validate it on the test data using the `fit()` function.
Make predictions on the test data using the trained model.
Save the predicted and actual values to a CSV file.
Plot a scatter plot of predicted vs. actual values (see the Python code).
